question: How many cumulative locally acquired human West Nile virus cases in Europe will ECDC report in its weekly surveillance update published on or around 18 September 2026?

calls.reasoning: Base: 1,086 across 15 countries in the 4 Sep 2026 update; the 18 Sep update adds roughly two reporting weeks (data to ~16-17 Sep). Reference-class ratio approach: Europe-wide two-week growth from the early-September to the mid-September cumulative was ~1.27 in 2025 (652 on 3 Sep, 989 on 3 Oct interpolated) and only ~1.14 in the record 2018 season (~1,317 on 7 Sep, 1,504 on 20 Sep), implying 1,240-1,380. Bottom-up by country implies ~1,420-1,440: Italy (516, ~48% of the total) is tracking its 2025 curve almost exactly (ISS 521 on 2 Sep 2026 vs 502 on 3 Sep 2025) and 2025 Italy added ~27% over the same window; Greece (284) is running at ~3x its 2024 full-season pace with a season that runs into late September; Spain, Romania, North Macedonia, Serbia and France all still climbing. Recent momentum is high (+461 over the two weeks to 4 Sep, ~230/wk) but onset peaks in mid-to-late August and reported increments typically crest 1-2 weeks later, so deceleration to ~150-190/wk is the central path. I land at 1,410, between the ratio and bottom-up estimates, with right skew for bulk retrospective submissions and first-time reporting countries (Turkiye and Hungary have both added large late lumps in past seasons). No human market prices this contract, so no crowd blend. Main counterargument to a high number: half the total is Italy, which decelerated sharply after early September in 2025, and the 2018 precedent shows big broad seasons can flatten faster than the recent slope suggests. Upside past 2,200 would require more than doubling in two weeks at a decelerating point in the season - above any full-season European total ever recorded - so priced at 1%.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: Resolves off the Europe-wide cumulative total of LOCALLY ACQUIRED human cases shown in ECDC's weekly human surveillance product 'Seasonal surveillance in humans in 2026 for West Nile virus' (dashboard at wnv-weekly.ecdc.europa.eu, linked from the ECDC WNV topic page), in the update published Friday 18 Sep 2026 - NOT the ECDC/EFSA monthly human-and-animal report (wnv-monthly.ecdc.europa.eu, different cadence and uses 'with known place of infection'), NOT the Italian ISS national bulletin, and NOT the CDTR. Travel-associated/imported cases excluded. Restated/revised earlier totals do not matter; only the figure displayed in the qualifying update governs. Fallback: most recent update published on/after 17 Sep and before 25 Sep 2026.

EVENT WINDOW: 2026 transmission season to date -> figure as displayed in the 18 Sep 2026 publication, per the criteria. calls.reasoning: Two independent methods converge. (1) Reference class: the ratio of the ECDC Europe-wide cumulative to the update exactly 14 days earlier, taken at the same seasonal phase (last weekly increment ~18-22% of the base), was 1.36 in 2022 (570->774), ~1.34 in 2018 (~844->1,134) and ~1.30 implied for 2025 (652 on 3 Sep -> 989 on 3 Oct); 1.33 x 1,086 = ~1,445. (2) Bottom-up: Italy's ISS increments (+86, +120, +89) and Greece's EODY increments (+75, +58) have both turned down from their late-August peak, while the ~15-country remainder ran ~65/week and includes late-peaking Spain and Romania; decaying at ~0.8/week gives Italy ~+150, Greece ~+90, rest ~+115, i.e. ~1,435. The main upside risks are lumpy batch submissions (2026 has already produced a ~+265 week; Serbia at 18 is far below its 2025 season total of 60 and could backfill) and the ~5-8% chance the 18 Sep product slips, in which case a later update covering an extra week governs. Downside is a faster post-peak collapse of reporting than 2018/2022 showed. Exceeding 2,200 would require the count to double in two weeks; priced at 1% for a redefinition/mass-restatement mechanism only.

BOTH-DIRECTIONS NOTE: increments in the two largest contributors (Italy, Greece) fell in the most recent reported week relative to the week before; at the same time the ECDC total's two most recent fortnightly increments were the largest of the season, the number of reporting countries has kept rising (7 -> 9 -> 12 -> 15 since 5 Aug), and several countries with historically late or lumpy reporting (Serbia, Spain, Romania) are currently at low counts relative to their own past seasons.

calls.reference_class: ECDC weekly Europe-wide cumulative locally acquired human WNV counts: two-week-ahead growth measured over the early-to-mid-September reporting window (approx. weeks 36->38) in the 2018, 2022, 2024 and 2025 transmission seasons

calls.reasoning: Base 1,086 (4 Sep update, data to 3 Sep); the 18 Sep update carries ~14 more days of reporting. Two methods converge: the same-phase two-week ratio class (1.30-1.36) gives 1,412-1,477, and a bottom-up build from national increments (Italy ISS +89 last week after +120, Greece EODY +58 after +75, ~15-country remainder ~+70/wk) decaying at ~0.85/wk gives ~1,428. Both largest contributors are past their weekly-increment peak, so decay is real - but 2026 is a late-shifted, unusually broad season (245 at 5 Aug vs a decade average of 403, then 15 countries and 20 newly affected areas by 3 Sep) with later-peaking Spain, Romania, Serbia and the Balkans still climbing, so the sharp 2025-style flattening is a poor template: Italy is 48% of this total, not 76%. Median 1,440, right-skewed for retrospective batch submissions and first-time reporting countries (Turkiye and Hungary have both added large late lumps in past seasons). No prediction market or bookmaker prices this contract - none found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or Metaculus - so no crowd blend. Exceeding 2,200 needs the count to double in two weeks on the descending limb, above any full-season European total but for 2018; priced at 1% for a mass-restatement or redefinition mechanism only.
calls.reconciliation: In dispute: (a) the 2018 two-week growth ratio - Run 1's 1.14x (1,317 -> 1,504) versus Run 2's 1.34x (844 -> 1,134). These are irreconcilable in a single scope: Run 1's 1,504 is EU 1,134 + neighbouring 370, so pairing it with an all-in 1,317 two weeks earlier would require the non-EU component to fall from 473 to 370, impossible for a cumulative. With no web access I could not determine which endpoint is misscoped or misdated, so rather than pick a side I dropped 2018 from the ratio class entirely and leaned on the 2022 observed pair (570 -> 774 = 1.36) and the 2025 monthly-implied ~1.30. This is the main reason my median sits above Run 1's: its low anchor did not survive. (b) The 28 Aug 2026 ECDC weekly total - unretrieved by all three runs, so the shape of the 21 Aug -> 4 Sep +461 is inferred, not observed; the ISS and EODY weekly series independently establish that the peak reporting week has passed, which is what the estimate actually rests on. (c) Pure judgment, decay rate: Run 1 read Italy's post-early-September 2025 collapse as the template; Runs 2-3 read 2026 as late and broad. No evidence breaks this cleanly, but Italy is 48% of the 2026 total against 76% in 2025, so the 2025 analogy governs less of the quantity - I bet on mild decay. I carried forward Run 2's reference class (same-phase 14-day ratio) minus its 2018 member, and set dispersion at 340 from 2026's own observed increment spread rather than from the reference-class SD, since the within-season series is the tighter evidence. All three runs and the harness searched for a market and found none; I retrieved nothing myself this run.

disagreements.claim: 2018 Europe-wide cumulative grew ~1.14x over the two weeks to 20 September (Run 1) versus ~1.34x (Run 2)
disagreements.verdict: Could not be settled without web access, but shown to be internally inconsistent - pairing Run 1's endpoints implies the non-EU cumulative fell 473 -> 370, which is impossible. 2018 dropped from the ratio class; the class now rests on 2022 (observed) and 2025 (implied).

disagreements.claim: The ECDC weekly cumulative on 28 Aug 2026 (the missing point between 625 and 1,086)
disagreements.verdict: Unsettled - no run retrieved it. Immaterial to the central estimate because ISS and EODY national weeklies independently date the increment peak to the week ending ~26-27 Aug.

disagreements.claim: Italy's decisive weight: does 2025's sharp post-early-September flattening transfer to 2026?
disagreements.verdict: Resolved against transfer on a factual ground - Italy is ~48% of the 2026 early-September total versus ~76% in 2025, so the Italy-driven template governs about half as much of the quantity.

disagreements.claim: Decay of weekly increments over the next two weeks: sharp (~0.7-0.75/wk) versus mild (~0.85/wk)
disagreements.verdict: No evidence breaks the tie. Took the mild reading: 15 reporting countries, 20 newly affected areas in the 4 Sep week, and later-peaking Spain/Romania/Serbia/Balkans still climbing.
